chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

While the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was among a group of his companions, a man came to him and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! I have had intercourse with a boy, so purify me.' He said to him, 'O you! Go to your house, perhaps your gallbladder excited you.'

So when it was the next day, he returned to him and said to him, 'O Commander of the Faithful! I have had intercourse with a boy, so purify me.' He said to him, 'O you! Go to your house, perhaps your gallbladder excited you.' He did that three times after the first.

So when it was the fourth time, he said to him, 'O you! Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged in a case like yours with three rulings, so choose whichever you wish.'

He said, 'And what are they, O Commander of the Faithful?' He said, 'A strike with the sword in your neck, reaching as far as it reaches, or being thrown from a mountain with hands and feet tied, or burning with fire.'

He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! Which of these is the harshest upon me?' He said, 'Burning with fire.' He said, 'So I have chosen it, O Commander of the Faithful!' He said, 'Prepare yourself for that,' so he said, 'Yes.'

So he prayed two cycles, then sat in his Tashahhud and said, 'O Allah! I have committed from the sin what You know of, and I feared from that, so I came to the successor of Your Messenger and the cousin of Your Prophet, and I asked him to purify me, so he gave me a choice between three types of punishment.'
O Allah! So I have chosen the harshest of them. O Allah! I ask You to make that an expiation for my sins, and that You do not burn me with Your fire in the Hereafter.'
Then he stood up while crying until he sat in the pit that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had dug for him, and he was seeing the fire blazing around him.

So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wept and all his companions wept. He said to him, 'Arise, O you, for you have made the angels of the sky and the angels of the earth weep, for indeed Allah has turned to you (with mercy). Arise and do not repeat anything of what you have done.'
ai.seo_question: What is the story of the man who chose burning as expiation for his sin in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of *kaffarah* (expiation) through symbolic physical suffering, where Imam Ali (AS) offers three severe penalties for a specific sin, and the man’s choice of burning leads to a miraculous spiritual purification. The weeping of the angels underscores the divine acceptance of his sincere repentance, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the Imam’s authority to administer justice and mercy. This event serves as a profound example of how physical acts can serve as metaphors for spiritual cleansing in Shia jurisprudence and theology.

en.hubeali: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ابْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ ابْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ بَيْنَا أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي مَلَإٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ إِذْ أَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنِّي قَدْ أَوْقَبْتُ عَلَى غُلَامٍ فَطَهِّرْنِي فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا هَذَا امْضِ إِلَى مَنْزِلِكَ لَعَلَّ مِرَاراً هَاجَ بِكَ Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Maalik Bin Atiyya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whilst Amir Al-Momineenasws was among a group of hisasws companions, when a man came over and said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws!
I have gone to a boy, therefore purify me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O you! Go to your house, perhaps your gall bladder is exciting you’.

So when is was the next morning, he returned to him<sup>asws</sup> and said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! I have gone to a boy, therefore purify me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘O you! Go to your house, perhaps your gall bladder is exciting you’. He did it three times after the first.

So when it was during the fourth, he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘O you! Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had judged regarding (a case) similar to yours with three judgements, therfore choose which of these you like’. He said, ‘And what are these, O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A strike with the sword in your neck, it reaches what it reaches, or throwing you off the mountain with your hands and feet tied up, or burning with the fire’. So he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>!

Which of these is the harshest upon me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Burning with the fire’. He said, ‘So I have chosen it, O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Are you prepared to take that, I<sup>asws</sup> shall call for you’. So he said, ‘Yes’.

So heasws said: ‘So he (the sinner) Prayed two cycles, then sat in his Tashahhud, so he said: ‘O Allahazwj! I had committed from the sins which Youazwj Know of, and I feared from that. So I went to the successorasws of Yourazwj Rasoolsaww, and a cousin of Yourazwj Prophetsaww, so I asked himasws that heasws should purify me. Soasws gave me a choice of three types of punishment.

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! So I have chosen the harshest of these. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> that You<sup>azwj</sup> Make that as an expiation of my sin, and that You<sup>azwj</sup> do not Burn me with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Fire in my Hereafter!’
Then he stood up and he was crying until he sat in the pit which had been dug out for him by Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, and he was seeing the fire inflaming around him.

So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> wept and his companions wept altogether. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Arise, O you, for you have made the Angels of the sky and the Angels of the earth to cry, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Turned towards you (with Mercy). So arise and do not repeat anything from what you have done’.
